claims.statement: 1951-01-30 UN First Committee adopted amended US draft by 45-7-8
claims.preciseConflict: FRUS d118 editorial note says 45-7-8; original A/1770 paragraph 18 says 44-7-8 and lists 44 affirmative states. Original 438th meeting facsimile unreadable. DO NOT silently choose one.
claims.nextOriginal: A/C.1/SR.438 scan roll call and A/C.1/659, compare facsimile numerals.

claims.statement: 1951-02-01 plenary resolution 498(V) adopted 44-7-9; Saudi Arabia is recorded as abstention despite declared nonparticipation
claims.preciseConflict: Not a discrepancy with 44-7-8 committee tally: separate date and body. Saudi Haliq's explicit nonparticipation is not a yes/no vote; Chair ruled abstention.
claims.nextOriginal: UN voting index and original roll call names.

claims.statement: Original US draft's 'rejected all UN proposals' survived into resolution 498(V)
claims.preciseConflict: UK Hansard reproduces original and revised text; final UN original says 'has not accepted'. Do not conflate text change with factual assessment of PRC diplomacy.

claims.statement: Allied consultations gave each UN troop-contributing government veto over crossing the 38th parallel
claims.preciseConflict: Rusk Feb 16 explicitly rejected an individual veto while promising consultations. Younger Mar 22 described consultation agreement for major advance, not veto rights.
claims.nextOriginal: UK Cabinet 14 Feb Bevin instruction and actual joint consultation records.

claims.statement: Truman's Feb 15 public description of crossing as military matter proves US approved political conquest of all North Korea
claims.preciseConflict: Public strategic authority, operational tactics, political reunification by force and ally consultation are different propositions.
claims.nextOriginal: JCS directives to MacArthur and presidential political instructions Feb-Mar 1951.

claims.statement: UK House of Commons 22 March speaker's Jan 30 'UN Assembly' date is the plenary adoption date
claims.preciseConflict: MP's retrospective Jan 30 phrasing corresponds to First Committee vote; plenary was Feb 1.
